_doc: Hand-maintained layer of the robot BOM (owner 2026-11-20: generated, but agents must be able to maintain and adjust it). robot/body/bom/build.py reads this file together with the selected body manifest and writes the BOM; every value here wins over the generated default and is marked `source: lines.json`. Edit it like any data file and commit. Sections: `lines` group manifest parts into one buy / make line (first match wins; `match` = part-name globs, `roles` = manifest roles, `motor` = the parts' manifest `motor` field) and carry what the CAD cannot know (supplier, part number, price, notes, make_buy: make | buy | included | context). Parts no line matches get a generated line: printed parts one line per part, standard hardware one line per spec (robot/body/bom/hardware.py), everything else one line per name stem (side prefix and trailing index removed). `manual_lines` are items with no CAD (filament, glue, wire). `part_overrides` move one part to another line, exclude it with a reason, or add notes. `quantity` on a line overrides the count from the CAD (the BOM shows both).

generated_line_defaults._doc: Fields for lines build.py generates (hw:<label>, sleeve:<size>) that no `lines` entry can carry without changing the generated grouping. Keys are globs on the generated line id, first match wins; `{name}` is the generated line name (for hw: lines the hardware.py label, e.g. 'M3 x 8 ISO 7380-1'). NOT READ by build.py yet: needs the overlay described in T-ghvncz (apply to a generated line's meta the first matching entry, only for fields it does not already have). No repo source names a supplier for standard hardware or steel sleeves (searched robot/, docs/, standard-parts.json), so supplier is 'unknown'.

rules.notes: Standard part: the designation is the part number (thread x length, head standard ISO 4762 / 7380-1 / 7045 / 10642, or ISO 4032 nut, from robot/body/bom/hardware.py). PA = thread-forming screw for plastics (robot/actuators/interfaces/standard-parts.json) with the named head form. Supplier: no repo source (unknown).
Washer size measured off ISO 7089 (hardware.py keeps it as measured); no standard designation, no repo source (unknown).
Spacer / standoff size measured by hardware.py; no standard designation in the repo, no repo source (unknown).
304 stainless tube cut to length, pressed in (robot/actuators/interfaces/standard-parts.json sleeve.material); no supplier or stock size in the repo (unknown).
